translations.text: But to whatever point we have reached, let us think the same thing and stand by the same rule.
Become imitators of me, brothers, and watch those who walk in this way, just as we are an example for you.
For many walk about of whom I have often told you, and now I tell you with weeping, about those enemies of the cross of Christ,
whose end is destruction, whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who think about earthly things.
But our citizenship is in heaven, from where we await the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ,
who will transform these bodies of our lowliness, so that they may be conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working of his power, and to subject all things to himself.
Therefore, my beloved and longed-for brothers, my joys and my crowns, stand firm in this way in the Lord, beloved.
I entreat Euodia and I entreat Syntyche to think the same thing in the Lord;

yes, I entreat you too, faithful yokefellow, help these women, who struggled together with me in the gospel, along with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are written in the book of life.
Rejoice always in the Lord; again I say: rejoice.
Let your humility be made known to all people. The Lord is near.
Do not worry about anything, but by every prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God,
and may the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, guard your hearts and your minds through Christ Jesus.

From now on, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honourable, whatever is just, whatever is holy, whatever is lovely, whatever is praiseworthy, whatever is virtuous, and whatever is commended, think about these things.
What you learned and received and heard and saw in me, do that; and may the God of peace be with you.
I rejoiced greatly in the Lord that now at last you have blossomed again in your concern for me. You were indeed concerned, but you were held back.
I do not say this to you because of any need, for I have learned to be content in whatever state I am in.
I know how to be brought low, and I know how to have plenty; in all things and in every circumstance I have been trained: to be full and to be hungry, to have plenty and to be in want.
I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
Yet you did well to share in these afflictions of mine.

And you yourselves also know, Philippians, that at the beginning of the gospel, when I set out from Macedonia, not a single church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving except you alone.
For even in Thessalonica you sent help for my needs once and again.
It is not that I seek the gift; rather, I seek the fruit that increases to your credit.
I have everything and I have more than enough. I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus what you sent: a fragrant aroma, an offered sacrifice pleasing to God.
And may my God fill your every need according to his riches in glory through Christ Jesus.
